scorecard.volMethod: Move size: the absolute open-to-close move of the next UTC weekday candle. Every model is run walk-forward on the replay days (only candles before each day; VIX with its FRED lag) and scored against the naive 20-day mean absolute move on MAE and QLIKE (ln h + r²/h, h = (π/2)·forecast²), on all days and on CPI / NFP / FOMC days (council/events.mjs). Models tried: evt (median of the last 24 same-type events × 20-day / 1-year vol), ewma (EWMA vol × event-day ratio), har (HAR-lite with event dummies), vix (VIX-implied, ES and NQ only); cur = the previous model, reference only. The rows are split at the middle date: a model is picked on the first half only if it beats naive on all four, and it is used only if it beats naive again on the second half. Otherwise the naive forecast is kept. dm* = Diebold-Mariano t of the loss gap (positive = better than naive).
scorecard.method: Walk-forward: each replay day uses only data published before it (FRED with publication lags, candles before the day); the score-to-probability map (anchored on the base up-rate, strongly shrunk, capped 35-65%) is refitted every 20 days on earlier days only (needs 120). Target: the next UTC weekday candle, up if close > open. Base rate = the share of the more common direction; coin flip (random walk) = 50% every day, Brier 0.25. Pesaran-Timmermann above 1.96 = direction calls better than chance. A 53% hit rate needs about 1,100 forecasts to tell from luck. The live log is append-only, written from 21:00 UTC before each day opens.

brief: Macro strategist, Fri 27 Nov 10:41 UTC, for Mon 30 Nov (UTC day, open to close). Regime: Dollar Smile left side (stress) · dollar liquidity rising · VIX curve inverted (stress). Gold: 53% up (base rate 53%; base rate, no macro tilt). Drivers lean up: real-yield 1-week momentum, risk sentiment; against: real yields. Expected move ±1.58% (20-day average). EUR/USD: 48% up (base rate 48%; base rate, no macro tilt, the replay finds no edge in its drivers). Drivers lean down: real yields, dollar smile regime; against: real-yield 1-week momentum. Expected move ±0.29% (20-day average). USD/JPY: 55% up (base rate 56%; macro tilt down 1 pt). Drivers lean down: us 10y yield trend, real-yield 1-week momentum; against: real yields. Expected move ±0.24% (20-day average). NQ (Nasdaq 100): 55% up (base rate 56%; base rate, no macro tilt). Drivers lean down: real yields, credit stress; against: real-yield 1-week momentum. Expected move ±2.01% (20-day average). ES (S&P 500): 53% up (base rate 54%; macro tilt down 1 pt). Drivers lean down: real yields, credit stress; against: vix term structure. Expected move ±1.35% (20-day average). DXY: 52% up (mirror of EUR/USD). Gold Macro Score -0.66 → AUCTION (no macro edge) (real yield 4w z -0.87, DXY 4w z -0.79, 2Y 13w z -0.63, curve 13w z -0.37; 6-week path -0.13 → +0.13 → +0.05 → -0.96 → -0.75 → -0.66; week to 2026-11-27; gold below its 10-week average). Direction only, never a sell; paper reading. No high-impact events in the next 5 days on the calendar we could read (next week's calendar is not published yet; it usually appears over the weekend). Honesty check: on the 880-day walk-forward replay the gold calls hit 53% against a 54% base rate (Brier 0.249 vs 0.25 for a coin flip, Pesaran-Timmermann 0.45): no proven edge (about the base rate). Treat the direction odds as context, not trade signals. Move size: all five markets keep the naive 20-day average: none of the 4 models tried beat it out of sample on both MAE and QLIKE, on all days and on CPI / NFP / FOMC days. CPI / NFP / FOMC days moved gold 0.991% on average against 0.876% on other days, but no model turned that into a better forecast.
